text: Shai, an American vocal R&B/soul quartet that gained prominence in the 1990s, formed on the campus of Howard University, influenced by the vocal styles of Boyz II Men, Jodeci, and Color Me Badd. The group was initially composed of Alpha Phi Alpha fraternity brothers Marc Gay, Carl Martin, and Darnell Van Rensalier, who invited fellow Howard University student Garfield Bright to join after two founding members left; none of the members had professional singing experience and primarily performed on campus for fun. They came together seriously after winning a Howard University talent show and decided to pursue a record deal in New York City, though they did not receive any offers. Martin gave Paco Lopez, a local deejay at WPGC radio in the DC metro, a demo cassette of "If I Ever Fall in Love," which he began promoting on the air. In September 1992, the group signed with Gasoline Alley/MCA Records and released their debut album later that year. The single "If I Ever Fall in Love," released as the first track from the debut album of the same name, peaked at number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and sold over two million copies. The subsequent singles "Comforter" and "Baby I'm Yours" each reached number 10 on the U.S. charts. At the group's insistence, the "Baby I'm Yours" music video was filmed on the Howard University campus, featuring actual Howard students, including future television host and model Ananda Lewis, as female love interests. Their next album, Right Back at Cha, was a remix album consisting mostly of new versions of their earlier hits and a few new songs, including a reworked version of "Baby I'm Yours" titled "Yours," which reached US No. 63. In 1993, Shai won an NAACP Image Award for Outstanding New Artist and performed at Bill Clinton's inauguration alongside Michael Jackson, Quincy Jones, Ray Charles, and Diana Ross. The group also appeared on The Arsenio Hall Show and The Tonight Show. In early 1994, they made a guest appearance on the sitcom "Family Matters" in the episode "Good Cop, Bad Cop" during a dream sequence. They released "The Place Where You Belong" from the Beverly Hills Cop III soundtrack, which was their final Top 40 single, peaking at No. 32 on the R&B chart. In late 1995, their follow-up album Blackface was released, reaching No. 42 on the Pop chart and No. 15 on the R&B chart; it included their final R&B Top 20 single "Come with Me," which reached US No. 43. The 1996 remix "I Don't Wanna Be Alone," featuring Jay-Z, peaked at No. 89 on the U.S. charts and was inspired by Belinda Carlisle's "Heaven Is a Place on Earth." The 2001 single "Song For You" by Rick Braun, featuring Shai, reached No. 39 on the R&B chart. As of 2025, Shai continues to perform together in various concerts and shows.
